To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermal stability of the back side metallization is strongly dependent on the diffusion of the metallization material.
thermal stability of back side metal layers is strongly dependent on the composition of the metal layers.
the thermal stability of back side metalization multilayers was investigated and the thermal stability of Ti/Pt/AU was confirmed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
thermal stability of back side multilayers for power devices.
the thermal stability of the metallization multilayers and die bonding material for the power devices.
the thermal stability of metallization multilayers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thermal stability of the multilayer is dependent on the metallization materials and their thicknesses.
Ti/Pt/Aulayer is the most promising metallization multilayers for power devices in terms of thermal stability.
Au paste with sub–micrometer Au particles is the most suitable die bonding material for power devices with high temperature aging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermal stability of the metallization multilayers was in good condition for high power device application.
the metallization multilayers are thermally stable at 300 ℃, but the metallization layer of Ti/Au should be avoided.
the metallization multilayers with high melting temperature metals are thermally stable at 300 ° for 300 h.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ti/Pt/AAu multilayer can be a candidate metallization layer to improve the thermal stability of the back side of the power device.
Ti/Ru/Ag/Ti/Au and Ti/Pt/Ag/Ti/Al/Au are promising back side metallization layers for the high temperature power device application.
the metallization multilayers with high melting point metal are thermally stable at 300 ℃ for long time.
